why: The hall's usher and its page come out of one `sequence`, at `at_ticks` 30 and 40, onto two marks. This edit takes the page's mark away and gives it the usher's: the usher is still standing there when the page is summoned, so the delve would put both bodies on one coordinate, inside each other. It declares no unit — an actor's `anchor` is a surface the primary already binds, and what the engine refuses is two live bodies holding one cell. What makes it worth committing is what the engine did with this shape before the refusal existed. A castle-tour campaign declared a captain of the guard and six men-at-arms all on `anchor/stop-gate`; the build exited 0 and emitted `summon minecraft:mannequin 77.5 68.0 40.5` seven times, one coordinate triple for seven bodies, with nothing said. On the ground the only thing separating them was that each `move-actor` walked off the mark at a slightly different speed, so the rank the author wrote came out as single file. The rule is co-existence, not a shared anchor: `actor/sergeant` and `npc/marshal` share `anchor/muster` in this same primary and are NOT refused, because the actor is never summoned and the npc takes the mark on its own — bodies that take turns on one cell are the handoff the engine supports. Perturbing toward the vacuous shape is the other direction of this probe: give the page back its own anchor and the gate goes green over a comparison it still makes, which the primary's binding line states as a count.
